evidence.text: The file page identifies 天-oracle.svg as a modern vector depiction of 天 in Shang oracle-script style and links its exemplar to Xiaoxuetang image 41.E045. The page states CC0 1.0. This verifies the image URL and provenance description; it does not establish the ancient graph’s meaning.
evidence.title: File:天-oracle.svg

evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: Oracle-bone and bronze records; editorial explanation
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone example 合集19050 and bronze example 集成02836. Its analysis says 天 depicts a frontal human figure with the head emphasized, later reduced to a horizontal stroke, and proposes extension from head to the sky above. This supports the review’s wording that 大 is the graphic basis for the person and the upper mark emphasizes the head, while remaining that database’s interpretation.
evidence.title: 漢字「天」：字形演變

evidence.source: 考古資料數位典藏創新計畫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The institutional explanation describes 大 as a front-facing standing person and identifies the upper mark as the person’s head, which is often simplified to a horizontal stroke. This independently supports separating the human-figure basis from the upper head mark; it is an explanatory analysis, not a direct transcription of a dated inscription.
evidence.title: 甲骨文 中與「天」相關的字

gaps: The image correction is established by the inspected Commons description, but the SVG bytes/image could not be opened in this web session, so its visible strokes were not independently inspected.

Academia Sinica’s head-marked analysis is editorial interpretation. It supports phrasing 大 as the graphic basis for the person and the upper mark as emphasized head, but does not resolve whether the earliest spoken sense was head/top or sky/heaven.
